targets.label: Cost reducer drawn (the deck's real curve fixer)
Payoff + a castable dragon by mid-game
Protection held for the big turn
Dragon-restricted mana drawn (counts for nothing in mana_analysis, everything for casting a Dragon)
A Treasure source drawn — seven in the 99, of which the model can SPEND only two
THE ENTRY KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a per-dragon DAMAGE payoff AND a way to put several Dragons on the battlefield at once
THE COMBAT KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a Dragon-damage MULTIPLIER AND a Dragon to attack with

engine.thesis: A five-colour Dragon deck that buys its own curve down and then taxes every Dragon that enters — one arrival multiplies into several, each arrival is priced in damage and cards — whose kill is PROVEN on a board and unproven as a board you can reach.

diagnosis.verdict: Above the mana line this deck is in good shape and the pilot is right about it: 12 interaction copies, 6 protection, 6 tutors, 4 finishers, and — once the audit's own probe list is read — about ten real card-advantage cards rather than the five the taxonomy sees. What limits it is the mana, exactly as the captain's log says: 31 lands against a 36-38 floor, 43 sources against Burgess's 45, and a land-drop rate that falls 0.834 / 0.670 / 0.525 across turns three to five while 26 of the 68 maindeck nonland entries cost five or more. The colour half of that is misread by the headline: the audit's -15 is black, and black is the colour this deck barely wants. Red carries 53.9% of the pip load on 30.0% of the sources. Separately, and not what binds: the conversion is better evidenced than a stack count suggests and both declared kills shrank under audit. TWO checker-passed, non-withheld boards are lethal — stack 001 (255 damage, both opponents on its board dead) and stack 002 (64 damage in 12 instances, the 32-life seat dead) — and both are entry-kill boards. Meanwhile correcting two mis-declared groups moved THE ENTRY KILL from 0.481 / 0.356 to 0.240 / 0.153 and THE COMBAT KILL from 0.411 / 0.290 to 0.204 / 0.128, so the entry kill is now both the better evidenced and the likelier plan — and it rests on a three-card damage leg.

open_questions.question: Stack 001 kills every opponent on its board, but its board assumes Ancient Gold Dragon has already connected in combat, and its d20 needs 12 or better rather than the 15 the scenario fixes (derived: three seats at 40 needs 3 x ceil(40/(N+2)) <= N, so N=12; nine faces of twenty). Build the reachable version of THE ENTRY KILL instead — Dragon Tempest or Terror of the Peaks or Scourge of Valkas, with a widener, and one nontoken Dragon cast — and resolve whether the cascade reaches three opponents at 40 or state the exact shortfall, as stack 002 does at 64 against 72.

Hellkite Courser's enters-the-battlefield trigger, one domain and three sub-questions: does it put The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone, does the haste it grants make an attack legal that turn, and does the return to the command zone at the beginning of the next end step add nothing to the commander tax under CR 903.8?

The Ur-Dragon's attack trigger with the commander on the battlefield: does 'whenever one or more Dragons you control attack' draw exactly one card per attacking Dragon, and may the permanent it then puts onto the battlefield from hand be any permanent card rather than a Dragon?

Scourge of the Throne, alone: does its 'attacks for the first time each turn' dethrone-conditioned trigger untap all attacking creatures and grant an additional combat phase, and is 'the player with the most life' re-evaluated in that second combat against life totals the first combat has already changed?

Given a second combat phase, do Utvara Hellkite's per-attacking-Dragon token trigger, Thrakkus the Butcher's power doubling and Atarka, World Render's double strike each fire again on the re-declared attackers?

Eerie Interlude with the entry payoffs on the battlefield: when the exiled Dragons return at the beginning of the next end step, do Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas and Lathliss each trigger again for every returning Dragon, and does Miirym copy the returning nontoken ones?

What does a goldfish target measuring the commander's ARRIVAL report — Hellkite Courser drawn, and Courser drawn with six mana available — separately from the nine-mana cast already reported at mean turn 8.172 and 4.1% by turn six?

Price the mana audit the pilot asked for after logged game 001, in the terms the goldfish can answer: with 9 basics against three basic/Forest-fetching sorceries and 14 of 31 lands entering tapped, what do mean available mana at turn five (4.219), the reducer-plus-ramp component (0.417 assembled / 0.285 by turn six) and commander-by-turn-six (4.1%) become if tapped lands are traded for untapped sources at constant land count? Scope caveat to state in the answer: the model reads land and ramp COUNTS, not enters-tapped status and not colour, so it can price one third of the pilot's question and must say so.

For strong Ur-Dragon lists, which is treated as the primary kill — the per-entry damage cascade (Dragon Tempest and Terror of the Peaks under Miirym and Panharmonicon) or a combat multiplier turn (Atarka, Thrakkus, an extra combat)? And where do those lists put their redundancy: more entry payoffs, or more combat effects and more ways to repeat a combat?

Does either checker-passed lethal board survive being made from a NORMAL position, and does either kill a 40-life seat? Both grant the hard part. Stack 001 kills both opponents on its board but grants Dragon Tempest and Ancient Gold Dragon already down, combat damage already dealt, and a d20 fixed at 15 against a median of 10.5. Stack 002 actually CASTS its Dragon, which is the shape this question wants, but grants four permanents already on the battlefield — Miirym, Panharmonicon, Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks — with eight lands, and its 64 damage kills the 32-life seat while the 40-life seat survives at 8. Resolve that same cascade with PANHARMONICON REMOVED — 002's exact board minus the doubler, which is the swap cut_candidates[5] proposes — and say two things: whether it is still lethal against the 32-life seat, and whether any version of it kills a seat at 40.

THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg is now three cards — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas — at 19.9% of openers, and deck-audit flags it thin. Is three enough for the deck's only rules-evidenced kill, and what in the pool or the format would join that leg? Re-measure with a widened leg against today's 0.240 assembled / 0.153 by turn six.

Re-goldfish the swapped list (31 lands to 36, five untapped or flexible sources in, six spells out) and report mean available mana at turn five (4.219 today), the turn-four and turn-five land-drop rates (0.670 / 0.525), and commander cast by turn six (0.041). Does five lands move them, and by how much?

What does the literature say about the floor on basic-land count for a five-colour Commander deck running Farseek, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim, Encroaching Dragonstorm and Fabled Passage — and running Prismatic Vista alongside them, as this diagnosis prescribes — at what point does whiff risk become material, and how does that trade against generic fixing?

Audit the mana base holistically for a five-colour dragon deck: is 9 basics the right count against the deck's land tutors, does the pip spread across the 22 nonbasic lands match what the dragons actually demand rather than being generic fixing, and are the 14 enters-tapped lands (5 always tapped) costing tempo where an untapped source would do? Black is the specific soft spot — 22% on-curve from lands alone, lowest of five colours, with no Swamp in the 99.

For a five-colour Commander deck with land tutors, what does the literature say about the floor on basic-land count — how many basics a Farseek/Nature's Lore/Skyshroud Claim package needs before whiff risk becomes material, and how that trades against generic fixing?

If land count and the ramp package were reshaped toward more untapped sources, how much would mean available mana by turn five (currently 4.219) and the commander cast rate (currently 4.1% by turn six, mean cast turn 8.172, never cast by turn ten in 7,170 of 10,000 iterations) actually move?

Which line, if any, is this deck's win line now? Three checker-passed stacks describe boards v1.0.0 can no longer make (003, 004, 006, all marked presentable: false) and the three that remain — 001 Dragon Tempest + Ancient Gold Dragon, 002 Miirym under Panharmonicon, 005 Sneak Attack — are not a proven kill.
